Internship Overview/Summary:
The purpose of this internship is to give college students hands-on exposure to the full AI lifecycle at FNB. This would include but not be limited to exploring banking use cases like fraud detection, credit risk, personalization, automation, and compliance monitoring to designing, training, validating, and testing machine learning and generative AI models. Interns will also gain practical experience in data engineering and MLOps, including data pipelines, cloud platforms, and model lifecycle management.
As an AI and Innovation Intern, you will apply your academic learning to real-world scenarios across the enterprise. You will gain hands-on experience in AI governance and responsible AI, including regulatory compliance, ethics, bias testing, security, and privacy in the banking domain. Interns will also collaborate with business, technology, cybersecurity, and compliance teams to understand how AI integrates into enterprise strategy and support vendor and tool evaluations to ensure alignment with the bank’s risk, security, and compliance standards.
Internship Duties and Responsibilities:
AI Use Case Exploration: Research and evaluate potential AI applications in banking, including fraud detection, credit risk modeling, customer personalization, automation, and compliance monitoring.
Model Development Support: Assist in designing, training, validating, and testing machine learning and generative AI models under the guidance of senior team members.
Data Engineering & MLOps: Support data pipeline development, cloud-based workflows, and model lifecycle management to ensure scalability and reliability.
AI Governance & Responsible AI: Participate in activities related to compliance, ethical AI, bias testing, privacy, and security to align with banking regulations and standards.
Collaboration & Teamwork: Work closely with business, technology, cybersecurity, and compliance teams to understand how AI integrates into enterprise strategy and operations.
Vendor & Tool Evaluation: Contribute to the assessment of third-party AI tools and platforms, ensuring alignment with FNB’s risk, security, and compliance requirements.
Research & Innovation: Stay updated on the latest AI trends, frameworks, and best practices, sharing insights that could enhance FNB’s AI initiatives.
Documentation & Reporting: Prepare reports, presentations, and documentation to support AI projects, findings, and recommendations for leadership review.
Learning Objectives:
As an AI and Innovation Intern, you will immerse yourself in cutting-edge AI applications and innovation within the financial services industry. By the end of the internship, you will be able to:
Drive real-world AI solutions: Apply machine learning, data analytics, and emerging AI technologies to live projects that shape business outcomes.
Collaborate with leaders: Partner directly with business and technical leaders on strategic initiatives, gaining insight into AI-driven decision-making.
Expand your professional network: Engage with experts across the organization through meetings, events, and cross-functional collaborations.
Accelerate your growth: Participate in targeted corporate training, workshops, and learning experiences to sharpen both technical and professional skills.

Become a part of our caring community
Join Humana as a Technology Intern for Summer 2027 and play an integral role in driving innovation and digital transformation within a Fortune 50 healthcare company.
Our 12-week internship program offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience across a wide spectrum of technological domains, contributing to projects that directly impact the health and well-being of millions. As a Tech Intern, you will collaborate with experienced technologists on initiatives that may include project management, agile development, software and cloud engineering, data science and analytics, user experience (UI/UX), machine learning, and cybersecurity. You will have the opportunity to leverage cutting-edge tools and methodologies to solve real-world challenges, build new skills, and make a meaningful impact in healthcare technology while launching your career at Humana.
The internship program is hosted in-person at Humana’s Headquarters in Louisville, KY, providing a rich experience of our corporate culture and direct mentorship from industry leaders.
Use your skills to make an impact
Required Qualifications:
Must be available to work full-time, 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday, on-site for the full 12-week internship program from May 24, 2027, through August 13, 2027, in Louisville, KY.
Must not require sponsorship to work in the United States now or in the future.
Must be a current full-time undergraduate or graduate student pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Data Analytics, Cybersecurity, or a related quantitative discipline.
Must have an expected graduation date between December 2027 - Summer 2028.
Must successfully complete CodeVue technical assessment requirements, which will evaluate programming fundamentals, problem-solving, and role-relevant technical skills.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience with technical tools, frameworks, and methodologies, including but not limited to C++, Java, HTML, SQL, C#, Python, Agile, project management, Scrum, data science, Power BI, Salesforce, JavaScript, CSS, cloud technologies, web/mobile development, API development, and AI applications.
Demonstrates strong academic performance, with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5.
Completion of introductory to intermediate technical coursework, such as CS 101, MIS, Foundations of Computer Science, Fundamentals of Computer Science, introductory programming courses, Data Structures, Algorithms, or Machine Learning.
Active involvement in on-campus and/or community activities.
Interest in working in the healthcare industry.
Possesses strong interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills.
Demonstrates intellectual curiosity, adaptability, and flexibility through previous jobs, internships, academic work, and/or projects.
Internship Program Overview:
During Humana’s 12-week internship program, interns can expect a structured and engaging experience designed to support both professional growth and meaningful project contributions. The program includes:
A comprehensive onboarding and orientation experience to help interns learn about Humana, the internship program, and their assigned team.
Placement on a technical team where interns can work closely with experienced leaders and team members, apply their skills, gain hands-on experience, and contribute to meaningful projects aligned to Humana’s mission, business priorities, and technology objectives.
Exposure to executive-level presentations, professional development sessions, and workshops designed to strengthen technical and career skills.
A strong support network that may include direct leaders, program managers, mentors, and peers throughout the internship experience.
Access to learning, training, and development opportunities that support both technical growth and professional development.
Opportunities to participate in intern-led committees and events, which may include initiatives such as Social Events, Yearbook, Volunteering, and other engagement activities.
Access to Humana’s Network Resource Groups (NRGs), which help foster connection, community, and inclusion across the organization.
Potential Team Placements:
Interns may be placed on one of several technical teams across the organization, depending on business need, skill set, and area of interest. Potential team placements may include:
CenterWell and Humana Military: The CenterWell and Humana Military IT organization provides technology to support Humana’s commitment of helping the millions of people we serve achieve their best health. The CenterWell area supports senior-focused primary care, home health, and pharmacy segments, while the Humana Military area supports military communities. Intern projects may include health system integrations, clinical support platforms, data interoperability, and digital tools that improve patient and provider experiences.
Data and Analytics: Delivers enterprise data, reporting, and analytics capabilities that help inform business and clinical decisions. Work may include data engineering, dashboard development, data quality improvement, and insights generation to support operational and strategic priorities.
Enterprise Growth and Digital: Develops digital tools, mobile applications, and self-service experiences that enhance member engagement, support business growth, and improve operational efficiency.  Projects may include building new digital experiences, implementing marketing automation, and using analytics to inform business strategy. 
Enterprise AI: Builds reusable, human-centered AI capabilities, tools, and services that support enterprise data science and high-priority business use cases. Work may include advancing AI solutions such as Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Conversational AI, model development, data pipeline optimization, and AI-driven insights for clinical and business challenges.
Enterprise Information Protection (EIP): Maintains the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Humana’s business, technical, and customer information for associates and members by complying with industry standards and prioritizing threat management. Projects may include cybersecurity, threat detection, vulnerability management, identity security, AI security, product security, data protection, risk and compliance, and secure cloud architecture.
Insurance Technology: Builds and supports the technology systems that enable Humana’s insurance operations and healthcare services. Projects may involve software development, cloud technologies, AI, automation, data engineering, and digital platforms that help deliver seamless member and provider experiences while advancing innovation and operational excellence.
CTO: Shapes the vision and roadmap for Humana’s technology landscape by aligning enterprise architecture, technology planning, and emerging technologies with business priorities. Interns may support technical research, AI enablement, enterprise architecture activities, IT framework development, and enterprise-wide technology transformation projects.
Humana does not provide visa sponsorship or support for OPT/CPT/J1 for this internship position.

Experience with Modern C++ software development.

Experience with large-scale datasets and quantitative algorithm evaluation.

Hands-on experience in AI, Computer Vision, Deep Learning, Image Processing, Modern C++, and Software Engineering.
End-to-end exposure to algorithm development, optimization, and deployment.
Experience building scalable, production-quality software.
Mentorship from experts in algorithms, imaging, software engineering, and semiconductor inspection.

At Lonza, we invest in great people. We encourage our employees to challenge themselves and we offer an environment that fosters creativity and success. Headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, we operate production, R&D, and business sites around the world, including Europe, North America, and Asia. 
At a Group level, we have established a company purpose to ENABLE A HEALTHIER WORLD. This is our reason for being. It is what motivates us to succeed and deliver for our customers and their patients, every single day. In fulfilling our purpose, we hope to achieve our Group vision to BRING ANY THERAPY TO LIFE.
Do you want to help us as we shape the future of this great organization?
Job Description Summary
We are actively recruiting candidates to participate in our 2027 On-site Summer Internship program. This program is roughly 12 weeks in length and will immerse you into the culture and operations of Lonza Portsmouth.
The Supply Chain Intern will support Scheduling, MRP Planning, Logistics, and Warehousing operations. This role offers hands-on experience with demand planning, SAP/ERP systems (via Michael Management training), and supply chain projects focused on operational excellence. The intern will assist with customer coordination, production scheduling, and inventory KPIs, while gaining exposure to tools like Access Orchestrate and contributing to weekly SAP reporting and master data management.
The internship program begins in May and ends in August. Potential interns must be able to commit to at least 40 hours per week throughout the duration of the summer internship.
Required Education
Completion of junior year (typically 90 credits) towards a B.S. degree in a related field
Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (out of 4) required
Must currently be enrolled in BS or MS Academic Program
Required Skills & Experience
Excellent verbal and written communications skills
Self-motivation and the ability to contribute as a team member
Ability to organize, plan and execute projects
Research skills and attention to detail
About Us
Lonza is one of the world’s leading and most-trusted suppliers to the pharmaceutical, biotech and specialty ingredients markets. We harness science and technology to create products that support safer and healthier living and that enhance the overall quality of life.
 
Not only are we a custom manufacturer and developer, Lonza also offers services and products ranging from active pharmaceutical ingredients and stem-cell therapies to drinking water sanitizers, from the vitamin B compounds and organic personal care ingredients to agricultural products, and from industrial preservatives to microbial control solutions that combat dangerous viruses, bacteria and other pathogens.
Further information can be found at www.lonza.com.
About Portsmouth
Our Lonza Portsmouth site is a clinical-to-commercial, multi-product manufacturing facility located in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, only 56 miles north of Boston, Massachusetts. The site, which employs over 1,500 employees, is a custom manufacturer of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and recombinant proteins using mammalian cell culture.
We offer an onsite cafeteria, fitness center and other amenities. The city of Portsmouth is home to many restaurants, museums, and theaters. The ocean and mountains are nearby, and we have major cities close by (Boston, Portland, Manchester).

Nonclinical Drug Safety helps advance high-quality drug candidates into development by defining the nonclinical safety and selectivity of lead compounds. Nonclinical Drug Safety employees evaluate Lead Op candidates and preclinical toxicity of drug development candidates, providing a mechanistic understanding of drug-induced toxicity and assessing implications for human safety. Nonclinical Drug Safety provides collaborative research in animal model development, veterinary medical and animal care, and research facility management. Nonclinical Drug Safety also responds to regulatory questions in support of drug registration.
The Digital Operations and Innovation (DOI) team within NDS Operations comprises a talented group of data scientists dedicated to leveraging scientific and operational data to reduce administrative burden, improve the findability and accessibility of data, and discover and implement innovative applications of AI to modernize and advance our business.
Position Overview:
We seek a talented and motivated Computer Science Co-op to join our team for a six-month role. This position will contribute to our efforts to develop an agentic, augmented authoring system supporting Nonclinical Drug Safety. The goal of this effort is to drive towards a "zero-draft" process that retrieves, combines, and formats key data from structured, semi-structured, and unstructured sources into a consistent template for our scientists. The ideal candidate will actively participate in regular sprints to design and refine agents, propose creative solutions to agent-based workflows, and work closely with scientific and operational SMEs.
In this role, you will be a valued contributor to a visible and necessary effort aimed at modernizing how nonclinical safety fulfills its critical role in the development of safe medicines for our patients. Your work will help produce stable, reliable, and consistent AI-driven pipelines that accelerate our reporting timelines and build technology at the cutting edge of our field.
The ideal candidate will have experience with the principles of Natural Language Processing (NLP) in addition to agent-based concepts including orchestration frameworks (such as LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, or equivalent), tool calling, and API integration. Strong Python coding and documentation skills are essential. Familiarity with AWS and Google services, GitHub, LLMs, and vector databases is an additional advantage. Familiarity with nonclinical drug safety, report authoring, and summarization is a strong advantage.
Key Responsibilities:
Design and implement agentic workflows and orchestration pipelines to automate the retrieval, synthesis, and formatting of nonclinical safety data.
Develop robust data extraction pipelines in Python to parse and clean structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data from diverse scientific sources.
Evaluate and benchmark LLM outputs for accuracy, formatting consistency, and alignment with strict nonclinical reporting templates.
Collaborate closely with fellow data scientists and scientific SMEs to translate manual document-authoring steps into automated, step-by-step agent tools and skills.
Participate in agile sprints, contribute to team code reviews, and maintain clean, production-grade documentation via GitHub.
Required Qualifications:
Education: Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, or a highly quantitative, research-focused field.
Programming: Strong proficiency in Python programming with a focus on clean, modular, and well-documented code.
Data structures: Solid understanding of data structures and proficiency in manipulating structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data.
AI & Orchestration: Hands-on experience working with LLM APIs, prompt engineering, agentic tool use, and orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, etc.).
Problem Solving: Strong analytical and research skills, particularly when dealing with noisy, unstructured, or ambiguous data sources.
Collaboration: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to bridge the gap between technical AI development and scientific domains.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience with vector databases and document embedding techniques.
Experience with text processing, OCR, and principles of NLP and NLP evaluation (ROUGE, BLEU, etc.).
Experience with cloud services (AWS/GCP) and version control using Git/GitHub.
Exposure to building lightweight developer UIs and dashboards for analytics and prototype/demo usage.
What You'll Gain:
Cutting-Edge Experience: Deep, hands-on experience building and deploying production-grade LLM agents and advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines.
Highly Valued Domain Knowledge: Practical knowledge of how to navigate enterprise data engineering and AI development within a secure, highly regulated healthcare environment.
Real-World Impact: A clear understanding of how modern generative AI accelerates drug safety reporting, directly shortening timelines to bring life-saving medicines to patients.
What We Offer:
Hands-on experience with cutting-edge AI and cloud technologies
Mentorship from experienced data scientists and software engineers
Collaborative and inclusive team environment
Potential for future full-time opportunities with our Company

Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Research in this internship will focus on scalable differentiable algorithms, including adjoint and automatic differentiation methods. The work will connect simulations with experimental data for calibration and data assimilation using AI/ML methods. These approaches will be evaluated on simulation workloads and assessed for integration into NVIDIA software used by researchers, engineers, and partner developers. If you enjoy working across mathematics, code, hardware, and engineering applications, we would love to meet!
What you'll be doing:
Prototype GPU-native solvers with adjoint and automatic differentiation techniques for engineering simulations.
Integrate AI-based methods with simulation algorithms for parameter calibration, inverse problems, and data assimilation using experimental or simulation data.
Co-design numerical algorithms and differentiation strategies for GPU parallelism, memory hierarchy, mixed precision, reduced synchronization, and distributed multi-GPU execution.
Evaluate numerical accuracy, convergence, gradient quality, performance, and scalability on workloads in CFD, mechanics, thermal systems, and multiphysics.
Identify promising methods and help move them toward reusable capabilities in CUDA-X libraries.
What we need to see:
Pursuing a PhD in applied mathematics, scientific computing, computational engineering, computer science, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or equivalent program area.
Strong foundations in algorithms related to PDEs, numerical linear algebra, iterative solvers, optimization, or scientific computing.
Research experience with adjoint methods, automatic differentiation, inverse problems, data assimilation, gradient-aware simulation approaches, or a related area.
Experience writing numerical software in Python and C++, with familiarity with parallel or GPU computing.
Ability to design computational experiments, evaluate numerical and performance tradeoffs, and communicate technical results clearly.
Ways to stand out from the crowd:
Experience developing, scaling, or analyzing GPU solvers, including multi-GPU or distributed execution.
Hands-on CUDA experience and use of profiling, benchmarking, or performance analysis to improve numerical algorithms.
Experience calibrating computational models or assimilating experimental data in scientific or industrial applications.
Experience with NVIDIA Warp, CUDA-X libraries, PyTorch, JAX, PETSc, Trilinos, MFEM, libCEED, OpenFOAM, or related computational science frameworks.
Publications, open-source contributions, or deployed research software in numerical methods, scientific computing, differentiable simulation, or computational engineering.

EDF internships provide high-quality experiences (including relevant projects and opportunities for networking) that form the foundation for any individual who is serious about pursuing an environmental career.
Location
U.S. Remote with option to be hybrid out of EDF’s office in New York City. Intern supervisor is in New York, and many team members are in across the United States.
Term
Spring 2027
Hours
Part-time (20 hr/week)
Application Materials
Interested applicants should attach their cover letter and resume to the EDF application.
Program/Department Overview
The Justice & Equity (J&E) team is a core capacity within EDF’s Mission. Guided by EDF’s Equity and Environmental Justice Vision and Principles and its Environmental and Climate Justice Strategic Plan, we work to embed environmental and climate justice frameworks across the Mission, optimizing EDF’s core strengths to drive lasting and effective environmental solutions.
Overall Function
EDF and Cornell’s Center for Conservation Social Sciences are conducting a research project that synthesizes research on inclusive and equitable technology, policy, and market-based approaches to climate and energy transitions. The team will translate key findings into practical criteria and actions for organizations like EDF to advance effective, inclusive and durable climate interventions in U.S. and global contexts. We will publish the results, create case studies, hold a workshop with partners to share the findings, and will integrate the criteria into EDF’s planning, training, and accountability processes. The intern will join the research team, led by Sr. Director for Just and Equitable Mission Engagement and report to Manager, Justice & Equity. Though the project will be completed after the internship period, the intern will play a key role in research, data analysis, and original writing and project planning.
Key Responsibilities
Tasks will include but are not limited to:
Research case studies that explore the impact of equitable decision making on environmental and climate justice initiatives. Case studies will focus on, but may not be limited to, infrastructure and policies related to the clean energy transition.
Synthesize case studies and provide a detailed report on internal and external initiatives and the impact of equitable decision making.
Work with the Frontline Resource Institute team to test and update its AI powered search engine for grants, testing it and writing feedback reports.
Prepare a strategic mapping of academic researchers and technical assistance providers to help inform an upcoming web series, develop a draft project plan.
Participate in advancing EDF’s organizational effectiveness and culture goals, so people from all backgrounds and experiences feel connected, included and empowered to address environmental and organizational challenges in ways that align with EDF values.
Qualifications
Demonstrated interest in research and environmental or climate justice.
Coursework in research methods, policy, or environmental studies recommended.
Experience or demonstrated interest in academic research and writing, including the ability to identify credible sources, review academic literature and policy materials, and organize findings.
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Suite.
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Must be well organized, motivated, and detail-oriented.
Ability to multi-task, prioritize and meet deadlines.
Ability to work in a team setting and have the ability to work independently when projects are due.
Demonstrate self-awareness, cultural competency and inclusivity, and ability to work with colleagues and stakeholders across all cultures and backgrounds.
Demonstrate initiative and problem solving skills.
Learn more about internships at EDF -http://www.edf.org/environmental-careers/internships

ABOUT POET
At POET, it is our mission to be good stewards of the Earth by converting renewable resources to energy and other valuable goods as effectively as humanly possible. For over thirty-five years, our drive and passion to change the world has enabled us to become the largest producer and marketer of bioethanol and a leader in sustainable products in the world.
CULTURE IS KING AT POET
We’re all on the same team. We always communicate. And we park our egos at the door. These aren’t just slogans on our walls. It’s the way we do things at POET. We provide an environment for team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance. It’s the best way to optimize health, wellness, and productivity in a sustainable way. We work hard. We play hard. We have frequent team events, volunteer efforts, and we know how to celebrate wins!
JOB SUMMARY & RESPONSIBILITIES
As an Animal Food Safety & Regulatory Intern, you will gain hands-on experience at the intersection of agriculture, science, regulatory affairs, and communication while learning how animal food ingredients are produced within the bioethanol industry.
You will work closely with Quality and Regulatory team members to learn manufacturing processes and translate technical animal food safety and regulatory concepts into engaging, practical training resources.
A key focus of this internship will be developing animal food safety training content and videos that bring food safety concepts to life for our team members. You will have the opportunity to visit bioprocessing facilities, interact with subject matter experts, learn how regulatory requirements apply in a manufacturing environment, and turn what you learn into meaningful educational content.
This is an on-site internship located at our corporate headquarters in Sioux Falls, SD. Responsibilities include:
Learn how POET's bioethanol production process creates high-quality animal food ingredients and other valuable bioproducts.
Partner with Quality, Regulatory, and other team members to identify important animal food safety concepts and training needs.
Research animal food safety regulations, industry guidance, and scientific concepts to support the development of accurate training materials.
Translate technical and regulatory information into clear, engaging content that is meaningful to team members.
Visit POET Bioprocessing facilities to observe manufacturing and animal food safety practices firsthand.
Develop scripts, visual aids, quick-reference materials, and other short educational training resources.
Interview subject matter experts and facility team members to capture practical knowledge and real-world examples.
Gain exposure to FDA animal food regulations, the Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA), Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs), and food safety plans.
Learn about programs such as sanitary transportation, pest management, chemical control, foreign material prevention, mycotoxin management, traceability, and product withdrawal and recall.
Collaborate across teams to better understand how regulatory requirements, quality programs, operations, and customer expectations work together.
Support additional Quality and Regulatory projects based on business needs and your areas of interest.
The POET Never Satisfied Internship openings are for Summer 2027. We post Internships in early September with the intention of having interns selected by November 1st.
QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS
You are currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Animal Science, Agricultural Science, Food Science, Biology, Chemistry, Agricultural Communications, Agricultural Business, or a related field.
You have an interest in animal agriculture, animal nutrition, food/feed safety, quality, regulatory affairs, or agricultural communications.
You enjoy learning about science and understanding the "why" behind processes and requirements.
You have strong written and verbal communication skills and can make technical information understandable to different audiences.
You are curious, organized, and comfortable asking questions.
You enjoy working with people and collaborating across different areas of an organization.
You are interested in creating educational content and communicating through presentations, videos, visual materials, or other creative formats.
Experience with PowerPoint, video editing, photography, graphic design, or other communication tools is beneficial but not required.
You are willing to travel to POET Bioprocessing facilities as needed to learn about operations and capture training content.
A SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE
Curiosity about how science, regulations, and agriculture come together in a real-world manufacturing environment.
Ability to translate complex scientific and technical information into clear, engaging, and easy-to-understand content.
Enthusiasm for creating educational content that can have a meaningful and lasting impact across the organization.
Strong interpersonal skills and a willingness to ask questions, engage with others, and learn from subject matter experts.
WORK ENVIRONMENT
Some travel will be expected for this position to visit the bioprocessing facilities.
In this role, you’ll be asked to drive a POET vehicle. A motor vehicle record check will be conducted during the pre-employment process.
This position operates in an office environment, working at a personal computer where you may sit or stand. Most of our Sioux Falls office workspace consists of an open-concept design intended to promote open communication and collaboration.
GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES
At POET, we encourage internal development and growth by allowing team members to carve their own path to success. Leaders support team members with the necessary resources to develop their skills, achieve goals, and create the most value. We believe in developing our team members to their highest potential and recognizing contributions that add value to the organization. Each new team member’s position and compensation are carefully determined by considering their unique qualifications and skillset.

A multifaceted wellness program encompassing the whole person – mentally, physically, and spiritually
On-site fitness centers or fitness reimbursements
Safety and cold-weather gear reimbursements

​As a Quality Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams:
Advanced Quality​
AQE interns work on engineering projects related to development of new products.  Areas of emphasis may include human factors engineering, risk management, application of statistics, reliability engineering, design verification, and design validation including customer interaction.  As Homer Stryker pointed out, “If your tools don’t work, make them work.  If you can’t make them work, make some that do work.”  In this directive, the AQE team works to make sure that the products we develop at Stryker will work consistently for our customers to meet or exceed their expectations.  ​
​​
Process Quality ​
PQE interns collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product sustainment. When non-conforming issues arise in production, it is our responsibility to perform robust root cause analysis and implement effective corrective actions.  Do you enjoy deep dive investigations and driving collaboration and communication to achieve issue resolution?  If so, you may be a great fit for this team!  PQE interns are focused on quality, compliance and continuous improvement.  They use their education to work with a variety of tools including CAD for fixture design, root cause analysis methods, LabView, and validation activities to optimize production, inspection, and quality system processes.  ​
 ​
Supplier Quality ​
SQE interns are responsible for all things supplier-related.  Stryker uses a number of critical suppliers to manufacture components and finished products, and to provide critical services.  This team’s job is to work closely with the suppliers to ensure components and their manufacturing processes meet our required standards.  Do you enjoy using your technical background and communication skills to influence suppliers?  If so, you might be a great fit for this diverse and talented team!  The role requires working closely with internal customers from multiple functions, meeting with suppliers frequently, and the use of both technical and business skills.   ​
​
Quality​
Quality interns work with our internal cross-functional teams and external sales team and customers to ensure we develop and sustain a product with the highest quality.  The team’s job is to ensure we develop the right products up front – evaluate risk, ensure our customer’s user needs are met, and help drive craftsmanship, safety, durability and reliability into the product.  On the post-market side, they also work closely with regulatory to handle any complaints and implement design changes, as needed, to address quality issues.  The role requires someone who has great communication, problem-solving, and technical skills.

As a Fortune 50 company with more than 400,000 team members worldwide, Target is an iconic brand and one of America's leading retailers.
Working at Target means the opportunity to help all families discover the joy of everyday life. ALL ABOUT OUR SUPPLY CHAIN OPERATIONS INTERNSHIP
Experience firsthand what it’s like to lead a team within a Target Supply Chain Facility. This internship is a paid 40 hr./week, hands-on training program to develop and prepare for your operations leadership. As an Operations Intern, you’ll gain a realistic job preview into life as an Operations Manager over a defined period of time. Within this Operations Management internship, you will work closely with other managers and team members in the building to develop an understanding of how Target’s supply chain business works and what it takes to excel in a management role. You’ll lead and support the execution of daily operations by working beside your team members and learn to lead, motivate and influence a team, including the opportunity to lead a department.
This program is designed to teach individuals how to lead within a supply chain facility. You will work closely with a Mentor as you take a deeper dive into how they effectively lead their department while gaining a line of sight into different business areas and functions within the building. You will spend your days learning how to problem solve, lead and motivate a team, conduct real-time observations, and drive results, all while ensuring safety is a top priority and that we are maximizing productivity to get products to the guest as fast as possible. During your internship, you will have the opportunity to step into leading your Mentors work center - of course, we will be there to guide you and help you learn along the way! Your development will be a top priority of ours, and to ensure you’re feeling supported, you can expect ongoing developmental conversations with your Mentor and Manager. We’ll be supporting you with extensive training to help you grow as a strong operations intern.
Hear more from past Interns, Mentors, & Managers here.
At Target, we believe in our leaders having meaningful experiences that help them build and develop skills for a career. The role of an Operations Intern can provide you with the:
Experience in building and managing a team culture across the building
Problem solving and change management skills
Knowledge of retail business fundamentals
Experience setting and planning department(s) daily/weekly workload to support business priorities and managing a team to deliver goals
Experience managing a team of hourly team members and creating business strategies and goals
Knowledge of departments within the distribution center that you will learn more about throughout the internship experience include- Inbound/Outbound/Warehousing
As an Operations Intern, no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will most likely include the following responsibilities:
Spending time on the facilities floor helping to lead amongst team members and aligning the team in daily business priorities.
Working alongside team members to lead through daily priorities
Maintaining a high standard of quality/inventory accuracy through standardization of processes (standard works, job breakdowns, and quality risk analysis) while also ensuring employee accountability.
Tracking various KPI’s such as safety, teamwork, quality and productivity to identify gaps, and drive actions in order to maintain consistent performance.
Carrying out process improvement initiatives by leveraging CI methodologies such as Gemba, Fish Bone Analysis, and 5 why’s to create a lean defect-free operation.
Administering the communication between the IT and the Operation team to address system issues and conduct testing in the WMS.
Recruiting and mentoring team members to adapt a continuous improvement mindset, and guide them to take up leadership roles in the company through engaging and inclusive leadership.
Addressing team member concerns and remove operational hurdles to ensure smooth operations and goal attainment.
Leading daily meetings for the operational team, share pertinent company and site-specific information.
Lead/present at daily planning meetings with peer/leadership team.
Plan daily goals and organize shift plans to achieve targets at start of shift.
Provide summary of results around plan attainment, share hurdles, successes, and key learnings to apply moving forward at end of shift.
Conduct audits around standard adherence with safety, quality, and productivity. Share feedback and coach team members on audit observations.
Conduct safety walks in building to identify, resolve and report findings.
Conduct follow-ups on team member attendance, any necessary coaching, etc.
Partner with leaders regarding team member performance by teaching, coaching, training, and delivering timely performance feedback
Provide new ideas and recommend solutions for business or team opportunities
Take the initiative to learn how to be a Target leader by seeking out opportunities for growth and development; continuously learn throughout the internship experience
Commit to learning Target’s expectations of leaders and use them to personally develop by asking questions and seeking feedback
Actively participate in internship program training activities, developmental opportunities, and events.
Demonstrate a willingness to take risks; step out of your comfort zone and take on new assignments
Demonstrate a culture of ethical conduct, safety, and compliance; lead the team to work in the same way and hold others accountable to this commitment
Foster an inclusive, safe, and secure culture
Carry out principle duties and responsibilities by the department through internship rotations as trained.
Understand business reporting and guest insights to understand, troubleshoot, and follow up on opportunity areas
Gain an understanding of all business areas to develop business acumen
Working with buildings leaders each day to set goals and expectations
About You
We might be a great match if:
•Working in a fun and energetic environment makes you excited… We work efficiently and as a team to deliver for our guests
• You enjoy the idea leading teams who are working to get products to our stores and guests… That’s the core of what we do
• If you aren’t looking for a Monday thru Friday job where you are at a computer all day… We are busy, oftentimes working different shifts in a 24-hour building getting merchandise to our teams and guests
The good news is that we have some amazing training that will help teach you how to be an effective leader within our facilities. But there are a few skills you should have from the get-go:
Participation in school or extracurricular activities and experience in leadership roles
Strong interest in working in retail, specifically within our supply chain facilities
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively
Problem-solving skills and strong initiative
Team-oriented thinking with enthusiasm for continuous learning
Ability to access all levels and areas of the facility to respond to team member issues.
Understand instructions, reports, and information
Climb up and down ladders
Scan, handle and move merchandise efficiently and safely, including frequently lifting or moving merchandise up to 15 pounds and occasionally moving merchandise up to 40 pounds
Flexible work schedule (e.g., nights, weekends, and holidays) and regular work attendance are necessary

Conference Supervisors are responsible for assisting with the planning for our upcoming 2027 summer conference season, as well as with the supervision of the summer conference operations team, coordination of event-related logistics, day-to-day operational tasks, information management, and record keeping in the conference software program StarRez. They will provide exceptional customer service and perform tasks related to summer programs including client communications, rosters, key and dining card management, room inspections, linen distribution if needed, and other relevant tasks. Conference Supervisors will also assist with the recruitment, hiring and training of our summer student team. They will lead and motivate that team throughout the summer and will be responsible for delegating work both in the office and out in the field. Conference Supervisors report to the Conference Operations Manager and Director of Conferences. This position is an office role during the spring semester but will also require time spent in our residential areas during the summer. Because our office is open 7 days a week from mid-May to mid-August, Conference Supervisors will be required to work a flexible hourly schedule, which will include assigned weekend rotations, some evenings and possibly holidays.
Qualifications:
Must be a full-time UVA undergraduate student in good standing.
Previous leadership experience is highly preferred.
Ability to work as a member of a team, motivate others and hold peers accountable.
Strong customer service, prioritization, and organizational skills required, along with demonstrated close attention to detail.
Self-motivated with capacity for self-directed work and problem-solving abilities.
Flexible, adaptable, and able to work in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to use word processing, spreadsheets, e-mail, and other software.
May be required to lift up to 25 pounds.
A valid U.S. Driver’s License with positive point balance preferred.
Conditions of Employment:
The Conference Supervisor is expected to work an average of 8 hours per week during the spring semester, starting Monday, February 8, 2027.
Beginning Saturday, May 15 through Monday, August 9, 2027, the Conference Supervisor will be expected to work an average of 35 hours per week.
The Conference Supervisor will be expected to participate in mandatory training on Saturday, May 15 and Monday, May 17.
The Conference Supervisor must commit to the entire spring and summer season, including the last week of summer (August 2 – August 9).
The Conference Supervisor must commit to a flexible work schedule, with summer hours expected to include some weekends, some evenings, and possibly holidays.
The Conference Supervisor may not have other commitments that interfere with their ability to perform the responsibilities of the position.
Time off must be pre-approved and is at the discretion of professional staff.
There will be no time off granted during the first and last week of employment.
Primary Responsibilities:
Information Management Duties:
Manage information in StarRez housing software, ensuring accurate guest data entry and continued maintenance of accurate client records for billing purposes.
Communicate with clients to ensure timely receipt of rosters, guarantees and other documentation.
Work with service partners to ensure dining needs and special requests are met, and facilities issues are addressed.
Operational & Supervisory Duties:
Supervise conference staff in preparing for conference group arrivals and departures.
Obtain and print rosters, labels, signage, and other program-related materials.
Manage linen inventory and lead and participate in its distribution as events require it.
Schedule, oversee, and participate in building inspections prior to and post conferences.
Organize staff transportation to and from check-in/out locations.
Coach, mentor, motivate, and support Conference Assistants in daily activities through example by active participation.
Participate in the summer staff hiring process by recruiting candidates, reviewing applications, interviewing and selection. Assist in the development and delivery of team member training.
Understand, comply with, and uphold University and Conferences@UVA operating procedures, policies, and philosophies.
Participate in regular weekly planning meetings with the leadership team and full team.
Collaborate with other Conference Supervisors to coordinate daily operations, identify needs, resolve issues, and ensure communication and follow-through.
Serve as the primary Supervisor on Duty during assigned shifts, providing overall operational oversight, delegate work to Conference Assistants and respond to issues.
Other duties as assigned.
Customer Service:
Serve as a conference expert for an assigned number of summer conference programs, working in tandem with professional staff to provide exceptional customer service to clients and guests, and ensuring proper record keeping of bed-nights and services for billing purposes.
Addressing client issues and concerns, and problem-solving as needed.
Work with assigned clients to obtain event details and ensure the successful execution of their programs through clear communication and delegation to team members.
Position Compensation:
Conference Supervisors are paid an hourly wage of $16.00 per hour during the spring semester, and $17.00 per hour during the summer.
They are also provided with free summer housing with access to kitchen facilities throughout the duration of their employment from May 29 – August 8 if needed. All residential facilities are smoke-free. Internet and utilities are provided. Washer/dryer units are available in the residence area, and staff are responsible for paying for their own laundry. All staff must provide their own linen, dishes, pots, pans, and other basic housewares during their stay. Successful applicants who do not opt for on-Grounds accommodations will not receive additional compensation in place of lodging.

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.
At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Visa's Internship Program offers a 12-week immersive experience where you'll work on impactful projects that advance Visa's mission. Support technology and business teams with planning, budgeting, and execution of strategic initiatives.
Analyze data from multiple sources to help create reports, dashboards, and business insights.
Assist with tracking technology assets, deployments, and inventory management activities.
Help evaluate technology demand requests and support business case development for infrastructure investments.
Partner with stakeholders to identify opportunities for cost optimization and operational efficiency.
Contribute to budget forecasting, spend tracking, and financial reporting activities.
Support creation of presentations and recommendations for technology and business leaders.
Participate in data analysis projects that help inform purchasing and investment decisions.
Gain exposure to technology procurement processes and financial governance practices.
Work cross-functionally with engineering, product, finance, and business teams on strategic initiatives.
Generative AI Responsibilities:
Utilize Generative AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar platforms to support research, analysis, and reporting.
Apply prompt engineering techniques to summarize information, analyze data, and develop business insights.
Identify opportunities to improve workflows through AI-enabled automation and efficiency gains.
Assist with GenAI-related initiatives that support business planning, financial analysis, and operational reporting.
Remember, at Visa, we see our employees as our most valuable asset and we are excited to support and witness your growth within our organization.
All Visa roles require digital fluency, including the ability to work with emerging technologies such as Generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot) to support everyday work.
Visa requires at least 3 days in office; expectations for these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Analytics, Finance, Economics, Information Systems, Information Science, Statistics, Business Administration, or a related field.
Graduating December 2027 - August 2028.
Ability to communicate clearly and professionally both verbally and in writing.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience working with data analysis and reporting tools such as Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or similar technologies.
Interest in financial planning, budgeting, business operations, technology strategy, or business analytics.
Ability to analyze data, identify trends, and communicate findings clearly through reports, dashboards, presentations, and recommendations.
Experience creating presentations and executive-ready materials for technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Interest in learning how large-scale technology organizations manage investments, assets, procurement activities, and operational costs.
Familiarity with Generative AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, or similar platforms.
Basic understanding of AI/ML concepts, Large Language Models (LLMs), prompt engineering, and emerging AI technologies.
Ability to leverage AI tools for research, data analysis, reporting, documentation, workflow automation, and productivity improvement.
Strong judgment in evaluating and validating AI-generated outputs for accuracy, quality, and business relevance.
Demonstrated curiosity, learning agility, and enthusiasm for applying data-driven and AI-enabled approaches to solve business problems.

Come build a career you believe in.
About the Role
Z Modular, a division of Zekelman Industries, is seeking a motivated Architectural Designer Intern to join our team for Summer 2027. This on-site internship opportunity is based in Troy, MI, and the official Zekelman internship program runs from May 24, 2027 through August 13, 2027. Reporting directly to the Architectural Project Manager, you will gain hands-on experience supporting the design and development of modular building solutions that help shape communities across North America.
Working alongside architects, designers, engineers, and construction professionals, you will contribute to architectural drawings, fabrication-focused shop drawings, and building code research while gaining exposure to how modular design integrates with manufacturing and on-site construction. This internship provides a unique opportunity to develop technical design skills, learn industry best practices, and gain real-world experience in an innovative and fast-growing segment of the construction industry.
The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, collaborative, and eager to apply architectural knowledge in a practical setting. This role is perfect for students who are excited about design, problem-solving, and seeing their work come to life through modular construction.
What You’ll Do
Assist in preparing architectural plans, sections, elevations, details, and other drafting tasks under the direction of a Project Architect.
Prepare shop drawings for plant fabrication using Revit.
Develop construction details for both shop installation and site-built conditions.
Research and identify products such as finishes and fixtures.
Research building codes and other standards for compliance.
Join team members for occasional on-site project observations in Arizona and Texas.
Provide solutions to daily design, sequencing, or integration challenges within the plant or on-site.
Promote safe and healthy work practices in compliance with company policy and regulatory standards.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Who You Are
Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Architecture or a related field.
GPA of 3.0 or higher.
Knowledge and experience with Revit.
Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Highly organized and detail-oriented with strong problem-solving skills.
Ability to adapt quickly in a fast-paced environment and manage competing priorities.
Collaborative team player with strong communication skills.
Available to travel for the Internship Summit, hosted at a Zekelman Industries location.
Authorized to work in the United States.
What You’ll Get
Zekelman Industries offers a PAID internship experience with meaningful work, professional development, and the opportunity to make a real impact. Interns also enjoy:
Hands-on exposure to modular design and construction processes.
Opportunities to collaborate with architects, engineers, and project teams.
Access to company-wide networking events, team-building activities, and learning sessions.
Regular coaching and feedback to support personal and professional growth.
Participation in a company-wide Intern Summit.
Zekelman Industries offers competitive compensation and excellent benefits, including low-cost, high-quality medical and dental benefits.  In addition, we have an amazing tuition assistance program, a bonus plan, a 401(k) plan with a generous company match, immediate vesting, and much more.
